    #EST S2 (2020 - 2021)

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    At t=0, θ=65​π=150°.

    rC​=r(cos150°i+sin150°j)

    rC​=0.2(65​π)(cos150°i+sin150°j)

    rC​=6π​(−23​​i+21​j)

    rC​=−123​π​i+12π​j

    x=−0.45345 m

    y=0.21680 m

    #Part (b)

    v=dtd​ 0.2θ=0.2ω

    vC​=r˙er​+rω˙eθ​

    vC​=ver​+rωeθ​

    vC​=(0.2ω)er​+(0.2θ⋅ω)eθ​

    vC​=(0.2⋅5)er​+(0.2π⋅5)eθ​

    vC​=er​+πeθ​

    vC​=12+π2​=3.2969 m/s

    θ=72.343° (w.r.t. positive er​ axis)

    vC​=3.2969 m/s ∠ 72.343+180°

    vC​=3.2969 m/s ∠ 252.34° (w.r.t. positive i axis)

    #Part (c)

    a=dtd​ 0.2ω=0.2α

    Since OA is rotating at a constant angular velocity, α=0.

    aC​=(r¨−rθ˙2)er​+(rθ¨+2r˙θ˙)eθ​

    aC​=(a−rω2)er​+(rα+2vω)eθ​

    aC​=[0.2α−0.2θω2]er​+[0.2θα+2(0.2ω)ω]eθ​

    aC​=−0.2π(52)er​+2(0.2)(52)eθ​

    aC​=−5πer​+10eθ​

    aC​=5πi−10j

    #Part (d)

    At θ=π, the pill rotates about some center O′ with a tangential velocity vC​.

    Thus, we have to find the components of aC​ in the direction of vC​.

    Let ut​ be the unit vector of vC​.

    ut​=cos252.34°i+sin252.34°j

    at​=aC​⋅ut​

    at​=(5πi−10j)⋅(cos252.34°i+sin252.34°j)

    at​=5π(cos252.34°)−10(sin252.34°)

    at​=4.7634 m/s2

    #Part (e)

    To determine the radius of curvature, we require normal acceleration an​.

    Thus, we have to find the components of aC​ perpendicular to vC​.

    Let un​ be the unit vector perpendicular to vC​.

    un​=cos(252.34°+90°)i+sin(252.34°+90°)j

    un​=cos342.34°i+sin342.34°j

    an​=aC​⋅un​

    an​=(5πi−10j)⋅(cos342.34°i+sin342.34°j)

    an​=5π(cos342.34°)−10(sin342.34°)

    an​=18 m/s2

    an​=rvC​2​

    r=183.29692​

    r=0.60382 m

    vC​=23​​ωBC​i+23​ωBC​j+vC/f​(−23​​i+21​j)

    101​=3(vC/f​−101​)+vC/f​

    101​=4vC/f​−103​

    vC/f​=0.1 m/s

    ωBC​=0

    aD​=αAD​k×(i+3​j)+0.1k×(−103​​i+0.1j)

    aD​=−3​αAD​i+αAD​j−0.01i−1003​​j

    αBC​=31​aC/f​

    −501​=−23​​αBC​−23​​aC/f​

    501​=23​​(31​aC/f​)+23​​aC/f​

    #Question 3

    9.81(4)=21​vs2​2+21​(5)vB2​2

    78.48=vs2​2+5vB2​2     −[1]

    Using conservation of momentum in the i-direction,

    (ms​vs1​+mB​vB1​)⋅i=(ms​vs2​+mB​vB2​)⋅i

    #Question 4

    #Part (a)

    Using conservation of linear momentum,

    mb​v1​=(mb​+mG​)v2​+mb​v2′​ (where v2′​ is velocity due to rotation about G)

    mb​v1​=(mb​+mG​)v2​+mb​rb/G​ω2​

    0.01(300)=10.01v2​+0.01(0.6)ω2​

    3=10.01v2​+0.006ω2​

    ω2​=500−1668.3v2​     −[1]

    Since linear momentum of the bullet acts away from the rod’s mass center G,
    it will create a moment about G and contribute to angular momentum.

    Using conservation of angular momentum,

    Hb1​=HG​+Hb2​

    mb​v1​rb/G​=IG​ω2​+mb​(v2​+v2′​)rb/G​

    mb​v1​rb/G​=IG​ω2​+mb​(v2​+rb/G​ω2​)rb/G​

    0.01(300)(0.6)=121​(10)(2)2ω2​+0.01(v2​+0.6ω2​)(0.6)

    1.8=310​ω2​+0.006v2​+0.0036ω2​

    1.8=0.006v2​+3.3369ω2​     −[2]

    Substituting [1] into [2],

    1.8=0.006v2​+3.3369(500−1668.3v2​)

    v2​=0.29938 m/s

    ω2​=0.53888 rad/s

    #Part (b)

    After initial impact, no external forces are applied, thus ω2​ is constant.

    θ=0.53888(1)=0.53888 rad

    #Part (c)

    When the rod engages the pivot O, the axis of rotation changes from G to O. Since axis of rotation changes, linear momentum of G contributes to angular momentum.
    Similarly, linear momentum of the bullet will also contribute.

    Initial Angular Momentum

    cos0.53888=0.6rb/G​​

    rb/G​=0.51497 m

    Hi​=IG​ω2​+mG​rG/O​v2​+mb​rb/O​(v2​+v2′​)

    Hi​=IG​ω2​+mG​rG/O​v2​+mb​(rb/G​+rG/O​)(v2​+rb/G​ω2​)

    Hi​=310​(0.53888)+10(0.5)(0.29938)          +0.01(0.51497+0.5)(0.29938+0.6⋅0.53888)

    Hi​=3.2695 kg⋅m2/s

    Note that rG/O​ refers to the perpendicular distance of v2​ to O.

    Final Angular Momentum

    cos0.53888=rG/O​0.5​

    rG/O​=0.58256 m (diagonal length)

    Hf​=IO​ω3​+mb​rb/O​v3′​ (where v3′​ is velocity due to rotation about O)

    Hf​=(IG​+mG​rG/O​2)ω3​+mb​rb/O​(rb/O​ω3​)

    Hf​=[310​+10(0.58256)2]ω3​+0.01(0.58256+0.6)(0.58256ω3​)

    Hf​=6.7340ω3​

    Note that rG/O​ refers to the diagonal length.

    Equating both sides of the equation,

    6.7340ω3​=3.2695

    ω3​=0.48552 rad/s

    v3​=vG​=rG/O​ω3​

    v3​=0.58256(0.48552)

    v3​=0.28285 m/s

    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    Since A rotates about O in a pure circular motion,
    the velocity of A is tangential to the crank rA/O​.

    rA/O​=rA/O​(−cos2θi+sin2θj)

    rA/O​=200(−cos60i+sin60j)

    rA/O​=−100i+1003​j

    vA​=vO​+ωAO​×rA/O​

    vA​=−10k×(−100i+1003​j)

    vA​=10003​i+1000j

    vA​=2000 mm/s ∠ 30°

    Vector in red is the resultant vector.

    Since A also rotates about C, it will have a component tangential to rA/C​.
    A also moves along the link BC, thus it will have a radial component vA/C​.
    Velocity vectors in blue are components of the resultant vector.

    Resolving vA​ on the blue axis,

    vA/C​=2000cos(30°+30°)=1000 mm/s

    vA′​=2000sin(30°+30°)=10003​ mm/s

    vA′​ is entrained velocity due to rotation about C.

    Using sine rule,

    sin30°200​=sin120°rA/C​​

    rA/C​=346.41 mm

    vA′​=ωBC​×rA/C​

    10003​j=−ωBC​k×−346.41i

    10003​=346.11ωBC​

    ωBC​=5.0043 rad/s

    #Part (b)

    Finding acceleration w.r.t. O,

    aA​=αAO​×rA/O​+ωAO​×vA/O​

    aA​=−10k×(10003​i+1000j)

    aA​=10000i−100003​j

    Resolving rA/C​, vA′​ and vA/C​ on the red axis,

    rA/C​=346.41(−cos30°+sin30°)=−300i+173.205j

    vA′​=10003​(cos60°i+sin60°j)=5003​i+1500j

    vA/C​=1000(cos30°i−sin30°j)=5003​i−500j

    Finding acceleration w.r.t. C,

    aA​=αBC​×rA/C​+ωBC​×vA′​+2ωBC​×vA/C​+aA/C​

    aA​=αBC​k×(−300i+173.205j)          −5.0043k×(5003​i+1500j)          +2(−5.0043k)×(5003​i−500j)          +aA/C​(cos30°i−sin30°j)

    aA​=−173.205αi−300αj          +7506.45i−4333.85j          −5004.3i−8667.7j          +23​​aA/C​i−21​aA/C​j

    aA​=(2502.15−173.205α+23​​aA/C​)i+(−13002−300α−21​aA/C​)j

    Comparing the i and j components,

    10000=2502.15−173.205α+23​​aA/C​

    23​​aA/C​=7497.95+173.205α

    aA/C​=8657.77+200α     −[1]

    −100003​=−13002−300α−21​aA/C​

    300α+21​aA/C​=4318.5     −[2]

    Substituting [1] into [2],

    300α+21​(8657.77+200α)=4318.5

    αBC​=−0.025942 rad/s2

    aA/C​=8652.6 mm/s2

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    Using Newton’s second law,

    mai=(mgsin30°−Fr​−Fcos30°)i+(N−mgcos30°−Fsin30°)j

    ai=(9.81sin30°−Nμk​−4tcos30°)i+(N−9.81cos30°−4tsin30°)j

    Comparing the j component,

    0=N−9.81cos30°−4tsin30°

    N=8.4957+2t     −[1]

    Using conservation of momentum in the i-direction,

    L2​=L1​+∫0t​ Fnet​ dt

    0=mv1​+∫0t​ mgsin30°−Fr​−Fcos30° dt

    0=5+∫0t​ 9.81sin30°−Nμk​−4tcos30° dt

    0=5+∫0t​ 4.905−0.5N−23​t dt     −[2]

    Substituting [1] into [2],

    0=5+∫0t​ 4.905−0.5(8.4957+2t)−23​t dt

    0=5+∫0t​ 0.65714−4.4641t dt

    0=5+0.65714t−2.2321t2

    t=1.6511s

    #Part (b)

    Using the restitution equation,

    vA2n​−vB2n​=−e(vA1n​−vB1n​)

    vA2n​−vB2n​=−0.3[5−(−8)]

    vA2n​−vB2n​=−3.9

    vA2n​=vB2n​−3.9     −[1]

    Using conservation of momentum in the en​-direction,

    mA​vA1​+mB​vB1​=mA​vA2​+mB​vB2​

    5+5(−8)=vA2n​+5vB2n​

    −35=vA2n​+5vB2n​     −[2]

    Substituting [1] into [2],

    −35=vB2n​−3.9+5vB2n​

    vB2n​=−5.1833 m/s

    vA2n​=−9.0833 m/s

    Negative signs indicate velocity towards the left.

    Fnet​t=L2​−L1​

    Fnet​=0.015(−5.1833)−5(−8)​

    Fnet​=1408.35 N

    #Question 4

    #Part (a)

    #Kinematic Analysis

    L=xA​+2xE​

    0=aA​+2aE​

    aA​=−2aE​

    Since a=rα for pulleys,

    αO​=−2αB​

    ωO​=−2ωB​

    ωB​=−21​ωO​

    Since C is attached to the mass center of B,

    aB​=rαB​=−21​rαO​=−21​aA​

    aC​=aB​=−21​aA​

    vC​=vB​=−21​vA​

    #Work and Energy Principle

    Let h be the change in height of C.

    W=ΔGPEA​+ΔGPEB​+ΔGPEC​+Rotational

    W=−mA​g(yA2​−yA1​)−(mC​+mB​)g(y2​−y1​)+∫0θ​ M dθ

    W=−mA​g(hsin30°−0)−(mC​+mB​)g(−h−0)+rh​(−M)

    W=−mA​ghsin30°+(mC​+mB​)gh−rM​h

    W=h[(mC​+mB​)g−mA​gsin30°−rM​]

    W=h[(mC​+mp​)g−mA​gsin30°−rM​]

    Note that h=rθ ⟶ θ=rh​.

    ΔKE=ΔKEA​+ΔKEB​+ΔKEC​+ΔKER,O​+ΔKER,B​

    ΔKE=21​mA​vA​2+21​mB​vB​2+21​mC​vC​2+21​IO​ωO​2+21​IB​ωB​2

    ΔKE=21​mA​vA​2+21​mB​(−21​vA​)2+21​mC​(−21​vA​)2               +21​IωO​2+21​I(−21​ωO​)2

    ΔKE=vA​2(21​mA​+81​mB​+81​mC​)+85​IωO​2

    ΔKE=vA​2(21​mA​+81​mp​+81​mC​)+85​(21​mp​r2)(rvA​​)2

    ΔKE=vA​2(21​mA​+81​mC​+167​mp​)

    Equating both sides of the equation,

    h[(mC​+mp​)g−mA​gsin30°−rM​]=vA​2(21​mA​+81​mC​+167​mp​)

    vA​2=21​mA​+81​mC​+167​mp​h[(mC​+mp​)g−mA​gsin30°−rM​]​

    Substituting into kinematic equation,

    vA​2=2aA​h

    2aA​=21​mA​+81​mC​+167​mp​(mC​+mp​)g−mA​gsin30°−rM​​

    aA​=mA​+41​mC​+87​mp​(mC​+mp​)g−mA​gsin30°−rM​​

    aA​=8mA​+2mC​+7mp​8[(mC​+mp​)g−mA​gsin30°−rM​]​

    aA​=8PA​+2PC​+7P8[(PC​+P)g−PA​gsin30°−rM​]​

    #Part (b)

    Using Newton’s second law on A,

    mA​aA​i=(TA​−mA​gsin30°)i+(N−mA​gcos30°)j

    PA​aA​i=(TA​−0.5PA​g)i+(N−PA​gcos30°)j

    Comparing the components,

    PA​aA​=TA​−0.5PA​g

    TA​=PA​(0.5g+aA​)

    #Part (c)

    Using Newton’s second law on C,

    mC​aC​=mC​g−TC​

    mC​(−21​aA​)=mC​g−TC​

    TC​=mC​g+21​mC​aA​

    TC​=PC​(g+0.5aA​)

    Using principle of angular momentum,

    IO​αO​=(TB​−TA​)r−M

    21​Pr2(raA​​)=(TB​−TA​)r−M

    21​PaA​=TB​−TA​−rM​

    TB​=TA​+21​PaA​+rM​

    TB​=PA​(0.5g+aA​)+21​PaA​+rM​

    Using Newton’s second law on B,

    mB​aB​=mB​g+TC​−TB​−TD​

    mB​(−21​aA​)=mB​g+TC​−TB​−TD​

    −21​mB​aA​=mB​g+TC​−TB​−TD​

    TD​=Pg+21​PaA​+TC​−TB​

    TD​=Pg+21​PaA​+PC​(g+0.5aA​)−PA​(0.5g+aA​)−21​PaA​−rM​

    TD​=Pg+PC​(g+0.5aA​)−PA​(0.5g+aA​)−rM​

    #Question 2

    #Part (i)

    rA/O​=300(cos0.5i+sin0.5j)

    rA/O​=263.275i+143.828j

    rP/A​=200(sin0.5i−cos0.5j)

    rP/A​=95.885i−175.52j

    rP/O​=rP/A​+rA/O​

    rP/O​=(263.275+95.885)i+(143.828−175.52)j

    rP/O​=359.16i−31.692j

    #Part (ii)

    Arm of the robot rotates as one rigid body about the hinge O.

    vP​=vO​+ωAO​×rP/O​

    vP​=0.25k×(359.16i−31.692j)

    vP​=7.923i+89.79j

    Note that vO​=0, thus vP​=vP/O​.

    Since f is located at the center, vf​=0.

    Note that vf​=ωf​×rf​, whereby rf​=0.

    vP​=vf​+vP/f​

    vP/f​=7.923i+89.79j

    #Part (iii)

    aP​=αAO​×rP/O​+ωAO​×vP/O​

    aP​=0.1k×(359.16i−31.692j)+0.25k×(7.923i+89.79j)

    aP​=3.1692i+35.916j−22.448i+1.9808j

    ap​=−19.279i+37.897j

    Similarly, since f is located at the center, af​=0.

    Note that af​=αf​×rf​+ωf​×vf​, whereby rf​=0.

    aP​=af​+aP/f​

    aP/f​=−19.279i+37.897j

    #Part (iv)

    Let P′ be a point that occupies the same position as P.

    vP′​=vf​+ωf​×rP/O​

    vP′​=0.35j×(359.16i−31.692j)

    vP′​=−125.71k

    Velocity due to rotation about the base points into the paper.

    #Part (v)

    aP′​=αf​×rP/O​+ωf​×vP′​

    Note that since ωf​ is a constant, αf​=0.

    aP′​=0.35j×(−125.71k)

    aP′​=−43.999i

    Normal acceleration due to rotation about the base points towards f.

    #Part (vi)

    acoriolis​=2ωf​×vP/f​

    acoriolis​=2(0.35j)×(7.923i+89.79j)

    acoriolis​=−5.5461k

    Coriolis acceleration due to change in radius from f points into the paper.

    #Part (vii)

    aP​=aP′​+aP/f​+acoriolis​

    aP​=−43.999i+(−19.279i+37.897j)+(−5.5461k)

    aP​=−63.278i+37.897j−5.5461k

    aP​=(−63.278)2+37.8972+(−5.5461)2​

    aP​=73.967 mm/s2

    #Question 4

    #Part (a)

    Let s be the distance travelled by C.

    Let h be the change in height of the mass center of A.

    h=s⋅sin30°=21​s

    Using conservation of energy,

    GPE=KEC​+KEB​+KEA​+Friction

    Friction between A and the slope does no work since there’s no relative motion.

    mA​gh=21​mC​vC​2+21​IB​ωB​2               +21​mA​vA​2+21​IA​ωA​2+FrC​⋅s

    mA​gh=21​mC​vC​2+21​(21​mB​rB​2)(rB​vC​​)2               +21​mA​vC​2+21​(21​mA​rA​2)(rA​vC​​)2+N2​μk​⋅s

    mA​gh=21​mC​vC​2+41​mB​vC​2               +21​mA​vC​2+41​mA​vC​2+mC​gμk​⋅s

    mA​gh=(21​mC​+41​mB​+43​mA​)vC​2+mC​gμk​⋅s

    Substituting in the given values,

    2mg⋅21​s=(21​m+41​m+43​⋅2m)vC​2+0.2mgs

    0.8mgs=2.25mvC​2

    vC​2=4516​gs

    Substituting vC​2 into kinematic equation vf​2=vi​2+2as,

    vC​2=2aC​s

    4516​gs=2aC​s

    aC​=1.744 m/s

    #Part (b)

    Since the cord is attached to the center of A,
    acceleration of the mass center of A is aG​=1.744 m/s.

    Using the principle of angular momentum,

    MG​=IG​αA​=IG​⋅rA​aG​​

    FrA​⋅rA​=21​mA​rA​2⋅rA​aG​​

    FrA​=21​mA​aG​

    N1​μs​=21​mA​aG​

    mA​gcos30°⋅μs​=21​mA​aG​

    μs​=0.10264 (Coefficient of friction for the slope)

    FrA​=N1​μs​

    FrA​=mA​gcos30°⋅0.10264

    FrA​=0.872mA​=1.7440m

    #Part (c)

    Analyzing A on its own, and applying work and kinetic energy principle,

    Friction between A and the slope does no work since there’s no relative motion.

    (mA​gsin30°−T)s=21​mA​vA​2+21​IA​ωA​2

    (mA​gsin30°−T)s=21​mA​vC​2+21​(21​mA​rA​2)(rA​vC​​)2

    (mA​gsin30°−T)s=21​mA​vC​2+41​mA​vC​2

    (mA​gsin30°−T)s=43​mA​vC​2

    Substituting vC​2=4516​gs into the equation,

    (mA​gsin30°−T)s=43​mA​⋅4516​gs

    mA​gsin30°−T=154​mA​g

    T=mA​g(sin30°−154​)

    T=2.289mA​=4.578m
